bull.b: Expected net interest income growth provides a durable earnings engine because it combines loan and deposit expansion with fixed-rate asset repricing. Management’s multi-year outlook also supports better operating leverage, giving the bank a stronger foundation for profitability over the next several quarters.

Strong wealth inflows, rising client balances, and double-digit revenue growth deepen a fee-based business that is less dependent on lending spreads. The scale of Merrill and private banking also supports cross-selling, recurring advisory revenue, and durable client retention.

A large and increasingly digital consumer franchise strengthens funding stability and expands opportunities to sell cards, investments, and other services. Continued checking-account gains and non-interest-bearing deposit growth can support lower funding costs and recurring customer revenue.

bear.b: The settlement directly reduced reported earnings and highlights ongoing remediation demands that can keep expenses elevated. Thousands of employees are involved, so the burden may persist beyond one quarter and reduce the operating leverage available from revenue growth.

bear.t: Higher Leverage and Lower Capital Ratio
bear.b: Higher leverage increases sensitivity to funding conditions and credit-cycle stress, while a lower CET1 ratio reduces flexibility for growth and capital returns. Uncertainty around final capital rules adds another constraint to future balance-sheet and shareholder-return decisions.

Dependence on market-sensitive businesses, particularly fixed income, makes revenue less predictable when rates rise or clients pause transactions. This cyclicality can offset strength in lending and wealth management and complicate sustained margin improvement across the firm.
